name: East Ridge

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble the ridge crest, generally linking clumps of trees, over an intimidating Class 4 step to a false summit, then downclimb into a notch and cross a crumbly Class 2 ledge above a big cliff (~290 ft, derived by subtracting the sourced 60 ft crux section from the 350 ft total route length).
About 60 ft of 3rd class leads to a well-protected, roughly 3-move low-5th-class crux just below the summit.

approach_variants.name: PCT past the Kendall Katwalk to a point due east of the summit, then straight up
approach_variants.notes:
From the PCT North trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass, about 3,000 ft, hike the PCT northbound past Kendall Pass and the Kendall Katwalk to Ridge Lake, then past Alaska Pass and around Alaska Mountain to Huckleberry Flats. The Commonwealth Basin shortcut rejoins the PCT and saves about a mile, and is the recommended line.

Walk on until you are essentially due east of Huckleberry's summit — roughly nine to ten miles in. That bearing is the trigger to leave the trail, not a named junction.

Many parties make this two or three days with a camp at Ridge Lake or Gravel Lake; a fit party has done it car to car in about eleven and a half hours.

About 17.4 km and 4,600 ft.
hazards: Stiff class 3 with class 4 moves on an exposed ridge — not a beginners' scramble
A loose block at the notch below the summit block
A crumbly class 2 ledge traverse above a big cliff
Rockfall in the alternative Beckey gully on the left, which has turned parties around
No simple walk-off: a 60 m rope is needed for the rappel off the summit block
A very long day, with parties commonly splitting it over two or three
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Leave the PCT when the summit is due west of you — a bearing, not a landmark, which is exactly what you want in cloud. From that point head cross-country west up steep heather or talus.

The base of the climb is where the mellow terrain ends and the ground turns rocky, at about 6,100 ft, marked by a rocky buttress. That change underfoot is the arrival, and it is felt rather than seen.

And then comes the one decision that decides which route you climb, which is the most valuable thing on this page. At the base of the rocks you have two options: left takes you into a steep loose gully leading to a notch and the summit block — that is the older Beckey line, and it has turned parties around with rockfall. Right takes you up the ridge on class 3+ terrain — that is the East Ridge, the historic first-ascent route, and it is what most parties now climb. If you are in a loose gully, you have gone left.

How to follow it once committed, because it does not look obvious from below: the route goes up the right side of the east ridge, essentially linking clumps of trees, tree patch to tree patch. Looking up at it, the line is genuinely hard to piece together by eye; once you start, the next move is usually clear. Staying towards the right is correct at the beginning.

Checkpoints higher up: about halfway, maybe a little further, leave the ridge proper by heading left on a short traverse to a blocky ramp, which you climb to a high point just before the summit block. Then descend about 20 ft to the notch at the foot of the block — either straight down, or skiers' right and a class 3 traverse to a ramp leading down to the notch.

The summit block itself: go up the middle to an obvious slabby ramp. From there either a short class 5 crack — one piece, a #1 Camalot at its start, is what the record describes — or follow the ramp climbers' left to exposed class 3/4. Bring a 60 m rope: a 30 m is insufficient for the rappel off the block.

Scale of the thing, so nobody underestimates it: there is no walk-up on this mountain, the scrambling is stiff class 3 with class 4 moves, and one of the 1915 first-ascent party wrote his will on his shirt cuff over doubts he would survive the descent.

approach: From the PCT North Trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass (~3,000 ft), hike the PCT northbound via Kendall Pass and the Kendall Katwalk to Ridge Lake, then continue past Alaska Pass to Huckleberry Flats (roughly 10-11 miles one-way with about 2,700 ft of gain to a camp). From Huckleberry Flats, leave the PCT and climb about 1,900 ft to the base of the east ridge at roughly 6,100 ft, where a rocky buttress marks the start of the technical ridge.
